items.title: 2026-022: Critical vulnerabilities in Nginx
items.summary: F5 disclosed five NGINX flaws allowing unauthenticated remote code execution as the worker process. CVE-2026-123007 was demonstrated by researchers; no in-the-wild exploitation yet. Patch internet-facing instances first.

items.title: OpenRouter Drops 3 Providers After Researchers Catch Months of Prompt Theft at AI Hosting Firms
items.summary: Dragos says attackers silently exfiltrated data from three AI inference providers for months, including prompts marked Zero Data Retention. OpenRouter removed the three providers from its routing pool.

items.title: Rackspace Spot breach let hackers access customer Kubernetes secrets
items.summary: Rackspace says attackers used compromised credentials to breach its Spot cloud platform, deploy unauthorized workloads and access Kubernetes secrets in customer clusters. Customers should rotate secrets.

items.title: Microsoft Entra Connect Health flaw exploited to steal tenant data
items.summary: Microsoft disclosed a breach after attackers exploited an Entra Connect Health vulnerability to access administrator email addresses and tenant configuration data.

items.title: Hackers Exploit Critical VMware, Cisco, and Apache Flaws as Espionage Attacks Emerge
items.summary: CISA added actively exploited flaws in Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver and VMware vCenter to its KEV catalog, including a CVSS 9.8 deserialization bug, amid emerging espionage activity.

items.title: 2026-021: High Severity Vulnerability in Java SE and OpenJDK
items.originalTitle: 2026-021: High Severity Vulnerability in Java SE and OpenJDK
items.summary: Oracle and OpenJDK fixed CVE-2026-114938, a high-severity flaw that can lead to unauthenticated RCE under certain conditions. CERT-EU advises prioritising internet-facing Java applications.

items.title: 2026-020: Critical Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway
items.originalTitle: 2026-020: Critical Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway
items.summary: Cloud Software Group patched 28 memory flaws in NetScaler ADC/Gateway; CVE-2026-120868 affects all deployments including default configs, with impact described as unpredictable behaviour and DoS. No known exploitation.

items.title: Researchers Demonstrate Ghostscript Sandbox-Escape RCE via Crafted File Uploads in Popular Apps
items.summary: Researchers at pwn.ai demonstrated a now-patched Ghostscript sandbox escape enabling RCE via crafted uploaded files, affecting Linux servers that convert user-supplied PDFs and images.

items.title: BADBOX botnet returns with record-breaking 40 billion daily ad requests
items.summary: The BADBOX botnet, embedded in generic Android TV boxes, has resumed large-scale ad fraud at a record 40 billion daily ad requests despite last year's takedown efforts.

items.title: Amazon: China-Linked Hackers’ AI Agents Exploited Medical Software Zero-Day
items.summary: Amazon reports a China-linked threat actor used autonomous AI agents to discover and exploit a critical zero-day in MONAI Label medical imaging software.

items.title: A Single Malicious Webpage Let Researchers Hijack Meta Muse and Access Private Chats
items.summary: Researchers showed a single malicious webpage could silently extract a Meta Muse user's private conversations, memories and potentially stored account credentials without approval prompts.

items.title: GnuPG Warns Critical GPGME Flaw Could Expose App Data via Malicious OpenPGP Keys
items.summary: GnuPG warns that CVE-2026-129975, a critical memory bug in GPGME triggered by malicious OpenPGP keys with long user IDs, could expose application data. Versions before 2.3.0 are affected; fixes available.

items.title: Attackers' AI Agents Found a Zero-Day in Medical-Imaging Software and Gained Root Access
items.summary: Amazon Threat Intelligence says suspected China-linked actors used autonomous AI agents to find and exploit a path traversal zero-day in MONAI Label 0.8.5 and earlier, gaining root on a university server.

items.title: 354 dark web vendors and buyers arrested in Europol-coordinated global crackdown
items.summary: Operation TorNado, coordinated by Europol across 14 countries from May 2025 to October 2026, led to 354 arrests of dark web vendors and buyers plus hundreds of house searches.

items.title: China opposes US FCC ban on Chinese telecoms' direct access to US phone numbers
items.summary: China objects to the US FCC's ban on Chinese telecom operators obtaining direct access to US phone numbers — a signal of continuing telecom supply-chain decoupling.

items.title: FBI Investigating Apparent Hack of Its Key National Criminal Justice Database, AP Source Says
items.summary: The FBI is investigating an apparent compromise of the national criminal justice database it maintains, according to an AP source.

items.title: FBI reportedly investigating apparent hack of its criminal database
items.summary: The FBI is reportedly probing a hack of the National Crime Information Center, a database shared by federal, state and local law enforcement.

items.title: FBI reportedly hacked again, this time targeting nationwide police database
items.summary: FBI systems were reportedly breached for the second time in two months, this time the National Crime Information Center used for inter-agency information sharing.

items.title: The Outages Are Just Getting Started
items.summary: Wired argues AI is accelerating exploitation of newly disclosed vulnerabilities, pressuring organisations into faster patching and driving more internet outages.

items.title: Russian ship damaged by drone attack in Gulf of Finland, Helsinki and Moscow say
items.summary: Finnish and Russian authorities report a Russian ship with ties to Russian armed forces was damaged by a drone attack in the Gulf of Finland, adding to Baltic tensions.

items.title: Russian threats ‘less and less hybrid,’ Von der Leyen says after assassination plot in Denmark
items.summary: Von der Leyen said Russian threats are becoming 'less and less hybrid' after Danish authorities disclosed a thwarted plot to assassinate a Ukrainian rapper in September.

items.title: Signal Blocks AI Agents From Reading Private Chats via Screenshots on Android and iOS
items.summary: Signal will restrict screenshots by default on Android and iOS to block agentic AI assistants from reading private chats, while admitting the protection is incomplete.

items.title: Over 70 women identified as victims of trafficking network operating across nine European countries
items.summary: Europol-supported actions on 5 and 19 November 2026 targeted a network trafficking Romanian women for sexual exploitation across nine European countries; over 70 victims identified.

items.title: Kenya’s internet metering bill raises privacy and affordability concerns
items.summary: Kenya's proposed internet metering bill raises privacy, surveillance and affordability concerns for connectivity — relevant context for telecom regulation debates.

items.title: Clashes erupt across France in another night of protest
items.summary: French police dispersed crowds during a sixth consecutive weekend of nationwide protests.

items.title: Iran war live: Iran targets US bases in Bahrain; Houthi strikes continue
items.summary: Iran struck US military assets in Bahrain and Houthi attacks continued, keeping Gulf tensions elevated.

items.title: Canada joins NATO innovation fund, promises ‘business as usual’ with US
items.summary: Canada joined the NATO innovation fund, framed as a response to reduced US cooperation while pledging continuity with Washington.

items.title: Effort to regulate ‘killer robots’ delayed to 2028
items.summary: International talks on regulating lethal autonomous weapons were postponed to 2028 after Russia and other states blocked progress.

items.title: President Trump Taps Kirsten Davies as National Cyber Director
items.summary: President Trump named Kirsten Davies as US National Cyber Director to drive an 'America First' cyber strategy.

items.title: Costa cuts proposed EU budget by €44B
items.summary: Council President Costa proposed cutting the EU budget by €44 billion, with Brussels planning a Big Tech tax to raise revenue for the next cycle.

items.title: Missing authorization in WeddingShare gallery media access
items.summary: WeddingShare through 1.8.2 exposes gallery item metadata through an endpoint that does not enforce the gallery secret. An unauthenticated attacker can use the disclosed information to access photos and videos from protected galleries when those files are served statically.
